steps.name: open_events_list
steps.purpose: Open the events list at /orders. Use this — not open_create — for any test about the list itself: its rows, filters, tabs, or the Create Event control.

steps.name: expect_events_list
steps.purpose: Assert the events list actually rendered: the Create Event control is present and no error is shown.

steps.name: expect_create_options
steps.purpose: Open the Create Event menu on the events list and assert which paths it offers. Use for any case about what a tenant is offered when creating an event (eRFX, single-stage, BOQ). Case-insensitive substring match per option.

args.options: array of option texts that MUST be present, e.g. ["eRFX","Single Stage"]
args.absent: array of option texts that must NOT be present (optional)

steps.name: expect_url_contains
steps.purpose: Assert the browser's current URL contains this text (a path, or a query parameter like projectCreation=true).

args.text: the substring the URL must contain

steps.name: filter_events
steps.purpose: On the events list, switch to a tab: Live, History, Drafts or Recurring.

steps.name: expect_event_in_list
steps.purpose: Search the events list by title and assert a matching row exists. Defaults to the title this plan gave its own event, so use it after publish or save_draft to prove the event is where the case says it should be.

args.title: title text to search for; omit to use this plan's own event title

steps.name: expect_event_status
steps.purpose: On the events list, find the event's row by title and assert its status label contains this text (e.g. Draft, Live, RFQ in Progress, Closed). Defaults to this plan's own event title.

args.status: status text the row must show
args.title: title to look for; omit to use this plan's own event

steps.name: expect_template_selected
steps.purpose: Assert the current stage has a template applied — the picker no longer offers 'Select Templates' — and, when a name is given, that the stage shows it.

args.name: substring of the expected template name (optional)

steps.name: expect_sheet_columns
steps.purpose: Assert the pricing sheet's header row has rendered from the template. With no args, asserts at least one column exists; with columns, asserts each named key is present (e.g. price, quantity, buyer_hub).

args.columns: array of header keys that must be present (optional)

steps.name: open_add_stage_menu
steps.purpose: On the create screen, open the "Add Stages" menu through its icon-only "+" button beside the stage tabs ("Add Stages" is the menu TITLE, never a button — do not click it). The menu lists only the stages that may still be added; a stage that may not be added is ABSENT (check with expect_hidden on its name), and the "+" tooltip says why (e.g. "Remove RFQ to add Auction"). With two stages the "+" is disabled. Leaves the menu open for expect_visible / expect_hidden / expect_text.

steps.name: expect_sheet_cells
steps.purpose: Assert which cells of the price / BOQ sheet (the data grid) a person can edit, read from the app's own locked-cell marking on the grid (nothing is clicked). Columns are named by their header text ("Product", "Quantity Requested", "Price", "GST", "Total Amount" …; the * is ignored). row = data row number, 1 = the first line item (the header row is never a data row). On an eRFX draft, cells filled from the line items (Product, Variant, Quantity Requested) and vendor columns (Price …) are read-only; Delivery location stays editable. Use for "product, quantity and variant stay read-only", "vendor cells are locked for the buyer", "only buyer columns are editable".

args.readonly: ["Product", "Quantity Requested", …] columns that must be read-only (optional)

steps.name: withdraw_event
steps.purpose: WITHDRAW an event, at any phase (live, after bids, after bidding closed, on any stage). The whole PROJECT is withdrawn from the project's ⋮ menu (the icon right after "Messages") → "Withdraw Project" → "Withdrawal Remarks" → "Yes, Withdraw Project"; one STAGE from that stage tab's Settings ▾ → "Withdraw" → "Please enter reason…" → Yes. Use for any "withdraw / cancel the event / project / RFQ / auction" in a case: scope "project" (default) for the event or project, "stage" when the case withdraws one round (e.g. "withdraw the RFQ stage"). noReason:true presses confirm with no remark — for cases that check the remark is required (the step reports Procol's refusal as blocked). Follow with expect_withdrawn.

args.stage: the stage tab for scope "stage": "rfq" | "rfp" (technical) | "auction" (optional; the first stage tab otherwise)
args.reason: the withdrawal remark (optional; a default is typed)
args.noReason: true to confirm with NO remark — a case about the remark being required (optional)

steps.name: expect_withdrawn
steps.purpose: Assert the event is withdrawn — read from Procol's own records (project or stage, as withdraw_event did), with the page's "Withdrawn" shown beside. Use after withdraw_event.

steps.name: event_menu
steps.purpose: Open the event menu that holds an action and choose it — for ANY of these words in a case: from the project's ⋮ menu (beside Messages): "Send Reminders", "Withdraw Project"; from a stage tab's Settings ▾: "Shared With", "Extend Submission Time", "Withdraw", "Convert to Auction", "Rejected Bids", "Order Activity", "Edit Evaluation Time", "Send Bulk Counter Offer", "Recreate Order", "Reschedule Event". The step goes to a stage tab when needed. What each opens (check THESE words, not the item's name): Shared With → a “Participation Summary” drawer (Invited · Seen · Bid Placed · Bid Not Placed); Order Activity → an “Activity” drawer (“You created the event …”); Send Reminders → a “Send Reminders” drawer (“Offer submissions” with “N Pending” and View — never press Notify, that messages the vendor); Rejected Bids → “Rejected Bids”; Edit Evaluation Time → “Edit Evaluation Time” (“Evaluation will end at …”). What the item opens (a dialog, drawer or popover) stays open for the next steps (expect_text on its words, click on its buttons, do_on_screen for the rest) unless close:true. Prefer withdraw_event, extend_submission_time, convert_to_auction or reschedule_event where they fit; this is for the rest. A greyed-out item fails the step — to CHECK it is greyed out use expect_menu_item{enabled:false}.

args.item: the menu item's words, e.g. "Order Activity"
args.close: true to close what it opened again (optional)

steps.name: expect_menu_item
steps.purpose: Assert what an event menu offers: open the menu that holds the item (project ⋮ or a stage's Settings), read it, close it. enabled:false — the item is there but greyed out (e.g. "Recreate Order" on a live RFQ, "Send Bulk Counter Offer" with no bids); present:false — the menu does not offer it (e.g. "Withdraw Project" after the project is withdrawn).

args.enabled: false when it must be greyed out (optional; default it must be enabled)
args.present: false when the menu must not offer it (optional)

steps.name: extend_submission_time
steps.purpose: On a published stage, Settings ▾ → "Extend Submission Time" → "Increase Event Time": choose "15 minutes", "30 minutes" or "an hour" → Ok. Use for "extend / increase the bidding / submission time". Returns the end time before the change and Procol's answer.

steps.name: add_price_cap
steps.purpose: On a published RFQ's or auction's Participants list, a vendor's "+ Add Price Cap" → "Add Price Cap for <vendor>" → a price cap on every product (the cap applies to the Net Price) → OK. Use for any "price cap" / "maximum price" / "ceiling price" for a vendor. Put it BEFORE the surrogate bid it should limit. With no vendor named, the first ticked participant. A case that checks a cap is required or must be positive: noPrice:true, or a price of 0 or below — the step then reports Procol's refusal as blocked. To check the cap was saved, follow with expect_price_cap (never do_on_screen).

args.noPrice: true to press OK with no cap entered (optional)

steps.name: expect_price_cap
steps.purpose: Assert a vendor's SAVED price cap: on Participants the row's "Add Price Cap" becomes "Edit Price Cap" once saved; the step opens it, reads every product's Price cap and closes WITHOUT saving. Use for "verify / check / inspect / confirm the price cap (is N)" after add_price_cap. With no price, the cap add_price_cap just saved.

args.price: the cap it must read (optional; default the one just added)

steps.name: expect_responses
steps.purpose: The BUYER's view of who responded on a stage, after vendors bid (place_bid from the vendor portal, place_surrogate_bid from the console): the stage's Responses tab, reloaded, has one column per vendor that responded — a surrogate one is tagged "Surrogate Bid", one from the vendor portal is not — and "Participation : x / y" (responded / invited). Same on an RFQ, a technical stage (RFP) and an auction. Use for "the buyer sees the response(s)", "both bids show for the buyer", "N of M vendors responded". On a two-stage event check each stage with stage:"rfp" / "rfq".

args.surrogate: how many are tagged Surrogate Bid (optional)
args.direct: how many came from the vendor portal — no Surrogate Bid tag (optional)
args.vendors: vendor names that must have a column (optional)
args.stage: "rfq" | "rfp" | "auction" — whose Responses (optional; default the first stage)

steps.name: extend_time
steps.purpose: On an event's page, open Settings → "Extend Submission Time" (which:"submission", default) or "Edit Evaluation Time" (which:"evaluation") and set the new time in the "Increase Event Time" window: option "preset" (a ready slot — the app offers "15 minutes", "30 minutes", "an hour"; preset = its duration e.g. "1 hour"), "custom" (amount + unit minutes|hours|days; direction "decrease" for Edit Evaluation Time's "Decrease by"), or "fixed" (at = "E+30m" = 30 minutes after the event's CURRENT END — use E whenever the case says "after / before the current end"; "+2h" = two hours from NOW; "-10m" = in the past). Presses Ok and judges the window's own answer; when it saves, reads the event's end before and after and checks the SUM (new end = old end + duration, or now + duration when bidding had already ended). expect "refused" for a negative case (also passes when the item is not offered, or is greyed out WITH a tooltip; message = words of the refusal). Use for every "extend submission time / edit evaluation time" case: by preset, by custom minutes/hours/days, to a fixed time, zero, empty, past time, before the current end, during live / evaluation / after award.

args.amount: number for custom (may be 0, empty, letters for negative cases)
args.confirm: false = fill but do not press Ok

steps.name: expect_settings_menu
steps.purpose: Open the event's Settings menu and check what it offers in the event's CURRENT state: offered (must be there), absent (must not be there), greyed (must be greyed out), enabled (must be clickable). Every greyed-out item must show a tooltip saying why (tooltips:false turns that check off). Use for "is X allowed when the event is upcoming / live / in evaluation / awarded" — e.g. after award: absent ["Withdraw"], greyed ["Extend Submission Time"].

args.tooltips: false = do not require tooltips on greyed items

steps.name: probe_controls
steps.purpose: EXPLORATION, not a check: click every control the current screen offers (buttons, tabs, menu items, links, switches), one at a time on the screen reloaded each time, and record what the app did — the dialog it opened (title, fields, buttons), the menu, the new page, the message, the request it sent, an error, or nothing; a greyed-out control is hovered for its tooltip. Never presses the confirm inside a dialog. Controls that usually change the event (Publish, Submit, Save …) go last. Use only when the case asks to find out what each control does ("what happens if I click …", "explore this screen").

args.within: "Settings" | "Actions" | "⋮ (more)" — probe the ITEMS of the menu this control opens, opening it again before each item (optional)
args.include: ["Settings", …] only controls whose name contains one of these (optional)
args.reload: false = do not reload between clicks (default reloads)

steps.name: expect_template_menu
steps.purpose: On the SINGLE STAGE create screen, open "Select Templates", read the name of every template the menu offers and close it without choosing. eventType (rfq | rfp | auction) switches the event type first; without it the type on screen is read. Checks the menu is not empty (min), names that must / must not be offered (contains / absent, matched as part of the name), and with distinctFrom that none of these templates is also offered for the other event type(s) — e.g. "RFP shows questionnaire templates, not the RFQ price templates" → {eventType:"rfp", distinctFrom:["rfq"]}. Use for "the template list matches the event type", "only RFQ templates are offered", "auction shows its own templates".

args.contains: ["Buy", …] parts of names that must be offered (optional)
args.absent: ["Questionnaire", …] parts of names that must NOT be offered (optional)
args.distinctFrom: ["rfq", …] event types whose templates must not appear here (optional)

steps.name: set_sheet_cell
steps.purpose: Type a value straight into one cell of the price / BOQ sheet (the data grid) like a person — click the cell (double-click if no editor opens), type, press Tab — and note what the cell shows afterwards. Columns are named by header text ("Quantity Requested", "Price", "GST" …). A locked (read-only) cell takes no typing; that is recorded, not failed. Follow with expect_sheet_cell to judge it. Use for "enter a negative quantity", "type letters into the price", "enter 0", "enter 1,00,000.555". For choosing a product use the product steps, not this.

steps.name: expect_sheet_cell
steps.purpose: Read one cell of the price / BOQ sheet and check it. kept:true = the value typed by set_sheet_cell stayed (numbers compared without separators, so "1,000" = "1000") and the cell is not marked as an error; refused:true = the sheet did NOT keep it (cleared, changed, locked, or marked as an error). equals / contains / empty check the text the cell shows. Use after set_sheet_cell for "the sheet does not accept negative quantity", "letters are not allowed in price", "the value is saved as typed".

args.kept: true = the typed value must stay (optional)
args.refused: true = the typed value must be refused (optional)

steps.name: open_event_settings
steps.purpose: On a published event's page, open its Settings (gear) menu — data-testid event-settings-button — and leave it open. It holds the event actions: "Reschedule Event" (only while the event is UPCOMING), "Convert to Auction" (published RFQ), "Extend Bidding Time", "Withdraw" and more. Use before click{role:"menuitem", name:…}; expect_visible / expect_hidden on menuitem names then checks what is offered. An item can be PRESENT BUT DISABLED (e.g. "Send Bulk Counter Offer" with one bid or fewer) — check that with expect_disabled{control: name}, not expect_hidden. A DRAFT reopens on its create screen, which has NO Settings menu at all: to prove an action is not offered on a draft, use expect_hidden{name} for that action on the draft screen — never click a "Settings" button there.

steps.name: reschedule_event
steps.purpose: On an UPCOMING event's page, open Settings → "Reschedule Event" (if the dialog is not already open), set "Make Order Live At" (date + time) and optionally the Delivery / Pickup Date, press Ok, and judge the dialog's own answer. Times are RELATIVE to now: start "+2h", "+1d", "-30m" — or to the event's CURRENT start with an S: "S+2h" (minutes round up to the picker's 5-minute step). The dialog's buttons are Cancel / Ok — never click "Save Schedule" here (that is the create screen). Refusals it shows: "Scheduled time is invalid!" (a past time) and "Schedule time should be on or before Delivery Date" (start after delivery); days before today are disabled in the calendar, which also counts as refused. expect "refused" for a negative case (add message for the words), "saved" (default) when it should go through. When it saves, the step also reads what the save SENT and checks the round keeps its length and its closing grace (against the window the API built) — keepsLength:false turns that off. It closes the dialog when it is done, so never follow it with expect_field_error / expect_message on a dialog field: put the expected words in `message`. A past DAY ("-1d") is greyed out in the calendar and counts as refused.

args.start: "+2h" | "-30m" | "+3d" from now, or "S+2h" from the current start (optional)
args.delivery: "+1d" relative day for Delivery / Pickup Date (optional)
args.confirm: false = set the fields but do not press Ok (optional)
args.keepsLength: false = do not check the round length / closing grace the save sent (default checks)

steps.name: expect_add_stage_options
steps.purpose: Assert what the create screen's icon-only "+" (Add Stages) menu allows, read from the menu itself (never use expect_visible / expect_disabled for stage names — the stage TABS carry the same names). disabled:true = the "+" is disabled (e.g. two stages is the ceiling); offers = stage names the menu must list; absent = stage names it must NOT list; reason = words the "+" tooltip must contain (e.g. "Remove RFQ to add Auction") — ONLY with disabled:true, since an enabled "+" has no reason. To check which stages are OFFERED, compose exactly ONE stage first — with two stages the "+" is always disabled.

args.absent: stage names that must not be offered (optional)

steps.name: open_stage_menu
steps.purpose: Open a stage tab's ⋮ overflow menu (Edit title / Delete …) and leave it open, so expect_disabled / expect_enabled can check its items. Defaults to the first stage tab.

steps.name: expect_disabled
steps.purpose: Assert a named control on the current screen is DISABLED (greyed out / aria-disabled). Use for rules like 'Save as draft is disabled until…', 'Delete is disabled while one stage remains', 'Savings is disabled before a template'. Matches buttons, menu items and tabs by their visible text.

args.control: the control's visible text, e.g. "Save as draft", "Delete", "Savings"

steps.name: expect_enabled
steps.purpose: Assert a named control on the current screen is ENABLED and clickable. The counterpart of expect_disabled.

steps.name: place_counter_offer
steps.purpose: Buyer side, on Master QCS after a vendor has bid: open the vendor's Counter Offer from their column header, enter a counter price in the drawer's sheet, add a remark and send it. The product offers the control only while the bid is live and active. Use open_master_qcs first. To CHECK Counter Offer is greyed out (e.g. on a surrogate bid) use attempt{step:"place_counter_offer", expect:"refused"} — the control sits in the vendor column's header, where expect_disabled does not look.

args.vendor: vendor name whose bid to counter (default: the first with a Counter Offer control)

steps.name: expect_counter_offer_sent
steps.purpose: Assert the comparison grid now marks the vendor's bid with a counter offer (the 'Counter offer initiated' mark).

steps.name: close_event
steps.purpose: On a PUBLISHED event's page, make the event CLOSED: Settings → "End <status>" (the product's force-end, where the tenant allows it) — otherwise wait for the bidding window to lapse. The product's shortest window is 30 minutes (set_schedule{minutes: 30}), so a wait costs about half an hour. This step IS the waiting: a case that says to wait for the window to close, expire or end uses close_event{natural: true} — never ask_tester. Use before cases that need a closed event (Master QCS on a closed event, awarding after bidding has ended, evaluating a technical stage — it is evaluated once its window has closed).

args.natural: true when the case says to WAIT for the window to close: never force-end it
args.maxWaitMinutes: how long to wait for the bidding window to lapse (default 36)

steps.name: open_event
steps.purpose: Open an EXISTING event — by project id (direct) or by title (search the events list and click the row) — landing on its project page. Returns to the event this plan created when it created one. When the case names no event and the plan creates none, leave id and title out: the run opens the Live events list and clicks the event that best fits the steps after it — one with bids in and bidding over for Master QCS, awarding and counter offers (its own test events first); one still open for quotes otherwise. No search. Never invent a title.

args.title: event title the case names (optional; leave out to return to this plan's event, or to let the run pick a fitting existing one)
args.purpose: "evaluation" when the case scores a vendor's technical response: the run picks an event whose TECHNICAL stage has closed with a vendor's answer waiting (optional)

steps.name: inventory_screen
steps.purpose: Record what the current screen offers — every button, tab, field, select, switch, column and banner, with disabled/required state — plus a screenshot and the accessibility tree. Asserts nothing. Used to write test cases from a screen; not for ordinary test cases.

args.label: short name for the screen, e.g. "create-erfx"

steps.name: create_new_version
steps.purpose: On a PUBLISHED event's project page (after publish + expect_published, or open_event), create a new version: "Create New Version" → confirm. The old version is archived and its bids become read-only; the create screen opens in edit mode on the copy, with the same stages, templates and line items. Follow it with the edits the case asks for (remove_line_items, add_line_items), then set_schedule and publish to publish the version. Only possible BEFORE any award proposal is submitted — never after award_event.

steps.name: remove_line_items
steps.purpose: On the create screen (a new version, or a fresh event before publish), delete line items in the Manage Line Items panel — each row's trash icon, confirm Delete — then Save. Removes from the end; at least one item must remain.

args.count: how many line items to remove

steps.name: accept_counter_offer
steps.purpose: VENDOR side: sign into the supplier portal as the vendor, open the event and accept the buyer's pending counter offer. Use after place_counter_offer. The vendor's view is a separate portal; when no Accept is offered, the step reports what that view shows.

args.vendor: vendor name (optional; the configured vendor identity is used)

steps.name: expect_counter_offer_accepted
steps.purpose: Buyer side, on the stage's Responses grid: assert the vendor's header now marks the counter offer as accepted.

steps.name: ask_tester
steps.purpose: THE PART OF THE CASE NO OTHER STEP CAN DO: put this step exactly where it belongs in the order (e.g. after publish, for "sign in as the evaluator and score the technical response") and keep every step you DO have before and after it. The run stops there and asks the tester in the chat for the steps or a login (another user, a second company…), then carries them out; if the tester skips it, that part is reported as not tested. Use it instead of returning no steps or guessing: never drop a case because one part has no step, and never mark such a case as covered. One ask_tester per missing part (at most one per plan: ask once, for the one thing the platform truly cannot do — a credential it does not hold, a screen it has never seen), and list the same part under cannotExpress. Never ask_tester to sign in or to open a list the steps can reach. Before it, use the steps that DO exist for everything around it — a vendor's technical response is place_bid (it answers the Technical Stage of a two-stage event), a closed round is close_event — and name in `need` ONLY what no step can do, in one short plain sentence ("sign in as the assigned evaluator and score the vendor's technical response"), never the parts other steps do.

args.need: the missing part in the tester's words, as a task: "sign in as the assigned evaluator and score the vendor's technical response"

steps.name: do_on_screen
steps.purpose: A PART NO OTHER STEP CAN DO, BUT ONE THE BUYER CAN DO ON SCREEN IN THIS SESSION (no other login, company, inbox or vendor portal): the run works it out in this browser itself, one action at a time with a screenshot each, and the step passes only when the screen proves the goal (then it counts as tested). If it gets stuck it asks the tester, as ask_tester does. Put it exactly where the part belongs in the order and keep every step you DO have before and after it. An event made from a PR is NOT this step: it starts with open_purchase_requisitions. Use ask_tester instead for anything that needs another user, another company, an email or the supplier portal.

args.goal: the part as a task with the screen it must end on: "open an approved purchase request and create an event from it; stop on the event's create screen showing the PR's line items"

steps.name: open_purchase_requisitions
steps.purpose: FIRST STEP of an event made FROM A PURCHASE REQUEST ("from a PR", "from the existing PR"): open Purchase Requisitions. Then pr_tab{tab:"Open"}, select_pr, purchase_items, choose_stages, expect_pr_items, each stage's steps (switch_stage when more than one, select_template, fill_questionnaires + assign_evaluator for Technical, fill_sheet for RFQ / Auction), then set_title, set_schedule, invite_vendor, publish. Never open_create or add_line_items for such an event: it is made from the PR and keeps its items.

steps.name: pr_tab
steps.purpose: On Purchase Requisitions, switch to a tab. Only an Open PR can become an event, so use "Open" before select_pr (never Completed, In Progress, Rejected or Deleted).

steps.name: select_pr
steps.purpose: Tick one PR's box on the current tab (the first row, or the PR the case names) and check that Purchase Items turns on. A case that wants "a PR with N line items" sets items: N — the step finds a PR with that many line items on the tab (each row is one line item) and ticks all of them.

args.pr: the PR number the case names (optional)
args.items: how many of one PR's line items to tick, for "a PR with 2 line items" (optional)

steps.name: purchase_items
steps.purpose: Click Purchase Items (never Actions) for the ticked PR, then Start New Project.

steps.name: choose_stages
steps.purpose: Pick the new event's stages and create it. Give `stages` ONLY when the case names the event ("technical event" → ["rfp"], "technical + RFQ" → ["rfp","rfq"]); with none the run asks the tester (Technical, RFQ, Auction, Technical + RFQ, Technical + Auction) and adds that event's stage steps itself. RFQ and Auction never go together.

args.stages: from "rfp" (technical) | "rfq" | "auction" — only what the case names (optional)

steps.name: expect_pr_items
steps.purpose: Assert the new event's create screen lists the PR's line items (the Items badge is above zero).

steps.name: capture_screen
steps.purpose: Record evidence of the current screen — a screenshot and the accessibility tree — under a label, without asserting anything. Use when a case wants to inspect or document a screen, or when the next thing to test has no step yet and a person needs to see the controls that exist.

args.label: short name for the capture, e.g. "order-details-counter-offer"

steps.name: open_participants
steps.purpose: On a PUBLISHED event's project page, open the stage's Participants list (the surrogate-bid drawer lives here). Reaching the list is the success condition — it is paginated and only eligible vendors show an Add Bid control. Reports how many rows offer Add Bid.

steps.name: open_master_qcs
steps.purpose: On a published event with bids, open the Master QCS tab and assert the comparison grid rendered with its line items and bidding vendors. Optionally name vendors that must appear.

args.vendors: array of vendor names that must be in the grid (optional)

steps.name: configure_single_stage
steps.purpose: On the SINGLE-STAGE create screen (open_create path single-stage), open the configuration drawer and set the event type; for an auction, its strategy and the awarding rule. This is where auction strategy is chosen on this build — rank, price or traffic light; knockout and dutch exist only through RFQ→Auction conversion.

args.awarding: "lot" (entire lot to one vendor) | "line_item" (partially, multiple vendors)
args.rangeLower: traffic light only: lower bound of the specified range (optional)
args.rangeUpper: traffic light only: upper bound of the specified range (optional)

steps.name: convert_to_auction
steps.purpose: On a PUBLISHED RFQ's project page (after publish + expect_published), open Settings → Convert to Auction and continue. The app opens the converted event's create screen in a new tab, which becomes the page for every later step. Knockout and dutch auctions are reachable only this way.

steps.name: open_create
steps.purpose: Open the event-create screen. Always the first step of a create test.

steps.name: compose_stages
steps.purpose: Set the stages exactly. RFQ and Auction cannot coexist; at most two stages. Auction is the default stage, so asking for anything else is a real change.

steps.name: set_title
steps.purpose: Type a title into the event's title box. LEAVE IT OUT when the case is about the AUTOMATIC title (auto title, "[RFQ] …", the title the app fills from the products / event type, "the title box stays empty"): typing one would replace what the case checks. When the case says to clear or edit the auto title, use the generic fill on "Enter the title of this event" instead.

args.title: string; omit to auto-generate a unique one

steps.name: switch_stage
steps.purpose: Move to a stage's tab. Required on a multi-stage event: template, sheet, questionnaires and evaluator all apply to the CURRENT tab only, so each stage must be configured on its own tab.

steps.name: select_template
steps.purpose: Pick the stage's pricing template. Required before line items can be added.

args.name: substring of the template name; omit to take the first offered

steps.name: add_line_items
steps.purpose: Add line items through the Manage Line Items drawer. NEVER after open_create{path:"boq"}: BOQ line items arrive by sheet upload only, which no step does — a BOQ case that adds items gets one ask_tester for the upload (or cannotExpress), never add_line_items.

args.search: optional product search text to use for all of them
args.quantity: optional — type exactly this value (as a string) into every added line item's quantity field, including an invalid one like a negative number or a letter, to test the app's own validation. Omit to let the automation fill a normal default.

steps.name: fill_sheet
steps.purpose: Fill the pricing sheet for every line item on screen.

steps.name: fill_required
steps.purpose: Fill every mandatory field still empty on the create screen (whatever this client makes mandatory — custom fields, Payment Terms, dates, dropdowns), on every stage tab. Publish already does this for a case that expects the publish to go through; use it alone only to say so explicitly.

args.said: optional — the app's refusal naming what is missing ("Payment Terms and Conditions are mandatory"); the control with that name is opened, filled and saved

steps.name: fill_questionnaires
steps.purpose: Technical stages only: give every RFI section (the global Vendor Assessment and one per line item) a template and fill blank questions.

steps.name: assign_evaluator
steps.purpose: Technical stages only: assign an evaluator to every control that needs one.

steps.name: set_schedule
steps.purpose: Open the schedule drawer and commit it. Needed before publish.

steps.name: invite_vendor
steps.purpose: Put vendors on the event. With no vendors named, the runner presses the product's own Invite Vendor and takes every vendor the products map to — the normal case. Name vendors ONLY when the test case itself names them (then each is searched for and added). count is EXACTLY the number the case says (“invite 2 vendors” = count:2) — never a spare: on a two-stage event the same vendors are on both stages, and one vendor may answer one stage by surrogate and another from the portal.

args.vendors: array of vendor names copied from the test case — omit unless the case names a vendor; never invent one
args.count: minimum number of participants required (e.g. 2 when two vendors must bid); QA test vendors top it up when the suggestion is short

steps.name: publish
steps.purpose: Publish the event and wait for the outcome.

steps.name: save_draft
steps.purpose: Save as draft instead of publishing. NOT on a single-stage screen (open_create{path:"single-stage"}): it has no Save as draft — for a case that asks to save one there, assert expect_count{role:"button", name:"Save as draft", count:0}, which is the product's answer.

steps.name: expect_line_items
steps.purpose: Assert the toolbar badge shows this many line items.

steps.name: expect_published
steps.purpose: Assert the browser reached a real project page with an id.

steps.name: expect_no_error
steps.purpose: Assert the application showed no error message.

steps.name: expect_error
steps.purpose: Assert the application DID refuse, optionally matching its wording. Use for negative tests.

args.contains: optional substring the message must contain

steps.name: place_bid
steps.purpose: Sign into the VENDOR PORTAL as a vendor on the event and submit a quote for the event just published. This is the vendor bidding for themselves. Each place_bid without a vendor signs in as a DIFFERENT vendor on the event (the next one with a portal login that has not bid yet), so two vendors bidding = invite_vendor{count:2}, then place_bid twice — no vendor names needed. On a Technical + RFQ (two-stage) event ONE place_bid does both: it answers and submits the Technical Stage, then quotes the RFQ at the price (seen 27 Oct, VB04) — never a second step or ask_tester for the quote. It IS the vendor's technical response an evaluation needs; if Procol keeps Submit Quote disabled after the technical answer, the step says so. The vendor portal opens BESIDE the buyer's page in the live view, and the buyer's page stays open: follow with expect_responses (the buyer sees it). A case where one vendor bids from the portal and the buyer enters a surrogate bid for ANOTHER: invite_vendor{count:2}, place_surrogate_bid with no vendor and place_bid with no vendor, in the case's order — the surrogate bid never takes the portal vendor.

args.vendor: optional: a vendor name the test case gives, or a number (1, 2, …) for the 1st, 2nd … vendor on the event; default: the next vendor that has not bid yet

steps.name: place_surrogate_bid
steps.purpose: Enter a bid FOR a vendor from the buyer console, without leaving it (surrogate bidding). Use when the test says the buyer bids on a vendor's behalf. Not available for knockout or dutch auctions. On a TECHNICAL stage the row's Add Bid opens the vendor's technical response, and the step answers it (seen 27 Oct on a technical-only event: Participants offer + Add Bid, no Add Price Cap). A price Procol refuses (0 or below keeps Submit Bid disabled) is reported as blocked — wrap it in attempt{step:"place_surrogate_bid", args:{price}, expect:"refused"}. A bid submitted with NO price: attempt{step:"place_surrogate_bid", args:{noPrice:true}, expect:"refused"}.

args.vendor: vendor name; defaults to the first vendor offering Add Bid
args.noPrice: true to submit with no price (a case about the price being required)
args.stage: "rfp" on a two-stage (RFP + RFQ) event to enter the vendor's TECHNICAL response on the Technical Stage; default the pricing stage (RFQ / auction)

steps.name: evaluate_technical
steps.purpose: EVALUATOR SCORING of a technical (RFP) stage, after close_event: the stage's assigned evaluator signs in to a tab of their own beside the buyer's (Procol lets only them score), gives each vendor's technical answer a score label (the client's list, e.g. Preference P1 / P2 / P3, On Trial, Technically Not Accepted - TNA) with a remark, and Submits each line item. Use for “score / evaluate the technical responses”, “as the evaluator …”, “submit the evaluation”. Always after close_event (scoring opens only in the evaluation time that follows); before award_event.

args.scores: optional: one label for every vendor ("Preference P1"), labels per vendor in column order, or numbers per vendor (higher = better label, e.g. [8, 6]); default the best label for all
args.remark: optional remark (required by Procol; a default is used)

steps.name: award_event
steps.purpose: Award the event after bidding: Master QCS -> Start Awarding -> allocate line items -> Create Proposal -> submit, ALL in this one step. Use it for ANY case that awards (“award the line / event to …”, “award in Master QCS”), after close_event; follow with expect_awarded (and approve_award when the case approves). Never start_awarding + expect_awarded for an award: start_awarding only enters the screen. Needs a closed event with bids.

args.vendor: whom to award: a vendor name the case gives, or "lowest" (Rank 1 on Master QCS — “the lowest bidder”), "surrogate" (the vendor the buyer bid for in this plan), "portal" (a vendor who bid from the vendor portal); default whichever bid can be allocated

steps.name: approve_award
steps.purpose: After award_event, approve the submitted award on its proposal page (remark + Approve), step by step, while the run's buyer is the pending approver. When another person is the approver, the case is reported as not checked.

args.remark: approval remark (optional; the app requires one)

steps.name: create_po
steps.purpose: After award_event, make the purchase order(s): approve the award to completion — the app then creates one PO per awarded vendor — and read the POs back. Use for "create the PO" / "raise a purchase order". Not available when the client makes POs through the custom PO form.

steps.name: expect_po_items
steps.purpose: After create_po, assert the purchase orders carry exactly the awarded line items (default: the event's current line items), each with a quantity; optionally a quantity every line must carry.

args.count: expected number of PO lines across all POs (optional)
args.quantity: quantity every PO line must carry (optional)

steps.name: start_awarding
steps.purpose: On Master QCS of a closed event with bids, press Start Awarding (or Bid Selection Proposal when a draft proposal exists) and land on the awarding screen. Use ONLY for cases about the awarding screen itself (its counters, allocating by hand); to award, use award_event.

steps.name: allocate_award
steps.purpose: On the awarding screen (after start_awarding), allocate the line items to a vendor and confirm the screen's counters moved. Use for cases about allocating / selecting a vendor for award; follow with expect_award_counters.

args.vendor: vendor name (optional; the first that can be allocated)

steps.name: expect_award_counters
steps.purpose: On the awarding screen, assert the counters read as given: "Tot. selected line items" items (e.g. "1/1") and "Awarded Vendors" vendors (e.g. "1/1").

steps.name: expect_awarded
steps.purpose: Assert the award went through (a proposal was created and submitted).

steps.name: expect_bid_submitted
steps.purpose: Assert the vendor's bid was accepted (the vendor portal shows the stage as Submitted).

steps.name: expect_publish_blocked
steps.purpose: Assert the event CANNOT be published yet: press Publish and confirm either the confirm button is disabled or the app refuses. Use for tests about a precondition not being met.

args.because: optional: words of the APP'S OWN message, never a paraphrase. Without participants the app says "Please add participants to proceed!" — and it checks participants FIRST, so a publish missing a template or line items is refused with that message too; a technical stage without an evaluator: "Please add Evaluator to all the line items in the Technical Stage"

steps.name: expect_stages
steps.purpose: Assert exactly these stage tabs are present.

steps.name: go_to
steps.purpose: Navigate to a screen that has no domain step: a published event's stage tab or one of its sub-tabs (responses, overview, participants, analytics, price trends, participant remarks), any tab by name, or a console path. Waits for the screen to be ready. Prefer open_events_list / open_event / open_create / open_master_qcs / open_participants when they fit.

args.screen: "stage" | "responses" | "overview" | "participants" | "analytics" | "price_trends" | "participant_remarks" | "tab" | "path" | "back" (the browser's back button) | "new_tab" (continue in the tab that just opened) | "url_on_screen" (open a URL that is written as text on the screen, e.g. in a mail preview; within = the text near it) | "events_list" | "event" | "master_qcs"
args.stage: for screen "stage": "rfq" | "rfp" | "auction" (optional; default the first stage tab)
args.name: for screen "tab": the tab's visible name
args.path: for screen "path": a console path such as "/orders" (no host)
args.title: for screen "event": the event title (default: this plan's own event)

steps.name: click
steps.purpose: Click an element named by role+name, label or text (e.g. the toolbar "Items" button, a menu item, a radio, a day in a calendar). Several matches: the first that can take a click (a covered or inert one is skipped). Fails if the element is not found or is disabled — use attempt{step:"click"} when the case expects the click to be refused.

args.role: ARIA role when it is a control: button | link | tab | menuitem | checkbox | switch | radio | textbox | combobox | row | heading | dialog (optional)
args.name: the control's visible name, exactly as on screen, e.g. "Items", "Add Bid" (with role)
args.label: a form field's label (instead of role+name)
args.within: optional region: "dialog" | "menu" | the text of the row/card it sits in

steps.name: hover
steps.purpose: Hover an element (to reveal its tooltip or menu). Pair with expect_message{kind:"tooltip"}.

args.role: ARIA role when it is a control: button | link | tab | menuitem | checkbox | switch | radio | textbox | combobox | row | heading | dialog (optional)
args.name: the control's visible name, exactly as on screen, e.g. "Items", "Add Bid" (with role)
args.label: a form field's label (instead of role+name)
args.within: optional region: "dialog" | "menu" | the text of the row/card it sits in

steps.name: fill
steps.purpose: Type a value into a field found by its label or placeholder (or role textbox + name), then confirm the field holds it. Also sets date/time/colour/number inputs (value as the input expects: YYYY-MM-DD, HH:MM, #rrggbb, a number), a range slider (the number), and chooses in a dropdown when the label is a select. A read-only field that opens a picker cannot be typed into — click the value in the picker.

args.label: field label or placeholder
args.within: optional region: the form, section, row or card the field sits in

steps.name: select
steps.purpose: Choose an option in a dropdown/select found by its label or its current text (native select, antd, a combobox or a button that opens a list, searchable lists), then confirm it shows the option.

args.label: the select's label, placeholder or current text (e.g. "Select a country")
args.option: visible text of the option to choose
args.within: optional region, e.g. the group "Ship from"

steps.name: toggle
steps.purpose: Set a switch or checkbox found by its label to on or off, then confirm its state. With only:true ("keep only Nonstop", "show only Paid") every other switch in the same group is turned off.

args.label: switch/checkbox label
args.only: true: turn the others in its group off (optional)

steps.name: upload
steps.purpose: Attach a file to an upload control found by its label/text (opens the file chooser or fills the file input), then confirm the screen shows it.

args.label: the upload control's label or text
args.file: a fixture ("sample.pdf" | "sample.png" | "sample.csv" | "sample.txt"), a path on the site under test ("files/orders.csv", fetched from it) or a URL

steps.name: press
steps.purpose: Press a keyboard key on the current screen (Escape to close a drawer, Enter to submit a search).

steps.name: expect_text
steps.purpose: Assert a text IS (present:true, default) or is NOT (present:false) visible on the current screen, optionally inside a region. An absence check waits for the screen to be ready first.

steps.name: expect_visible
steps.purpose: Assert an element (by role+name / label / text) is visible (visible:true, default) or absent (visible:false). Use for 'the drawer opens', 'no price drawer', 'the Recurring toggle is shown'.

args.role: ARIA role when it is a control: button | link | tab | menuitem | checkbox | switch | radio | textbox | combobox | row | heading | dialog (optional)
args.name: the control's visible name, exactly as on screen, e.g. "Items", "Add Bid" (with role)
args.label: a form field's label (instead of role+name)
args.within: optional region: "dialog" | "menu" | the text of the row/card it sits in

steps.name: expect_count
steps.purpose: Count visible elements matching role+name / text and assert count (exact), min or max — e.g. zero "Add Bid" buttons, at least 1 row, exactly 2 stage tabs. Count 0 / max 0 is an absence check and waits for the screen to be ready.

args.role: ARIA role when it is a control: button | link | tab | menuitem | checkbox | switch | radio | textbox | combobox | row | heading | dialog (optional)
args.name: the control's visible name, exactly as on screen, e.g. "Items", "Add Bid" (with role)
args.label: a form field's label (instead of role+name)
args.within: optional region: "dialog" | "menu" | the text of the row/card it sits in

steps.name: expect_value
steps.purpose: Assert the value a field/select/radio group SHOWS — the input's value, the select's chosen option, the checked radio — found by its label. Case-insensitive contains.

steps.name: expect_message
steps.purpose: Assert the app shows a message of a kind — toast, error, warning, success, inline (form error), tooltip, modal — optionally containing text. For a tooltip, give `on` (the element to hover). Reads toasts that already faded via the run's toast journal.

args.on: for tooltip: the visible name of the element to hover, e.g. "Items"

steps.name: remember
steps.purpose: Read and keep the text of an element or region under a key, so a later expect_remembered can compare (e.g. the line items before a rename).

args.role: ARIA role when it is a control: button | link | tab | menuitem | checkbox | switch | radio | textbox | combobox | row | heading | dialog (optional)
args.name: the control's visible name, exactly as on screen, e.g. "Items", "Add Bid" (with role)
args.label: a form field's label (instead of role+name)
args.within: optional region: "dialog" | "menu" | the text of the row/card it sits in

steps.name: expect_remembered
steps.purpose: Re-read what remember{key} read and assert it is the same (same:true, default) or changed (same:false).

steps.name: switch_tab
steps.purpose: Continue the plan in another browser tab: the one that just opened (default), or the tab whose title or URL contains the given text. Use when a click opens something in a new tab.

steps.name: pick_date
steps.purpose: Choose a date in a calendar picker: opens the field named by its label, turns the calendar to the right month (its next/previous buttons or month/year selects), presses the day. For a plain date input it types the date. Use for any check-in / departure / date-of-birth field that opens a calendar.

args.label: the date field's label (optional when the calendar is already open)

steps.name: choose_by_number
steps.purpose: Compare the blocks on screen (rows, cards, list items) by a number each shows — a price, a unit price, hours, a rating — and press a control in the lowest or highest one: "add the cheapest pack", "click the cheapest result that is not Sponsored", "open the longer-lasting model". Reports the numbers it compared.

args.measure: "price" (default: a money amount) | "number" | a regex with one capture group for the figure, e.g. "([\d.]+)\s*hours"
args.only: only blocks naming this, as whole words, take part — e.g. "Voltpine Alkaline AA" keeps the AA packs and not the AAA ones (optional)
args.exclude: blocks containing this text are left out, e.g. "Sponsored" (optional)
args.within: optional region: "dialog" | "menu" | the text of the row/card it sits in
args.role: ARIA role when it is a control: button | link | tab | menuitem | checkbox | switch | radio | textbox | combobox | row | heading | dialog (optional)
args.name: the control's visible name, exactly as on screen, e.g. "Items", "Add Bid" (with role)
args.label: a form field's label (instead of role+name)

steps.name: scroll_to
steps.purpose: Scroll the page (or the scrollable list/table on it) until an element named by role+name or text comes into view — for long pages and lists that load more as you scroll. Fails if it never appears.

args.role: ARIA role when it is a control: button | link | tab | menuitem | checkbox | switch | radio | textbox | combobox | row | heading | dialog (optional)
args.name: the control's visible name, exactly as on screen, e.g. "Items", "Add Bid" (with role)
args.label: a form field's label (instead of role+name)
args.within: optional region: "dialog" | "menu" | the text of the row/card it sits in

steps.name: drag
steps.purpose: Drag one element (a list row, card or handle named by its text) and drop it on another, before it by default; confirms the list changed.

args.from: text of the element to drag
args.to: text of the element to drop it on

steps.name: dialog
steps.purpose: Arm the answer to the NEXT browser dialog (alert / confirm / prompt) BEFORE the click that opens it: accept or dismiss, with optional text for a prompt. Pair with expect_dialog to assert what it said.

args.text: text to type into a prompt (optional)

steps.name: expect_dialog
steps.purpose: Assert that a browser dialog appeared since it was armed and, optionally, that its message contained a text.

args.text: substring the dialog's message must contain (optional)

steps.name: expect_download
steps.purpose: Assert that the browser saved a file during this plan and check its contents: the file name, text it must contain or must not, its data-row count (CSV/log: lines below the header), or a JSON path's value. Works for text, CSV, JSON, logs and simple PDFs.

args.name: the file name expected, e.g. "orders.csv" (optional: the newest download)
args.contains: text or array of texts the file must contain (optional)
args.notContains: text or array of texts the file must not contain (optional)
args.rows: expected number of data rows below the header (optional)
args.eachRow: text every data row must contain, e.g. a status (optional)
args.json: a JSON path such as "orders[2].status" (optional, with equals)
args.equals: the value the JSON path must equal

steps.name: switch_company
steps.purpose: Sign the console in as another QA test company (by company id) and reload — for cases comparing tenants. Only known QA tenants are allowed; never changes any setting.

args.companyId: numeric company id named by the case (e.g. 32461)

steps.name: skip
steps.purpose: NEGATIVE TESTS ONLY: mark a mandatory step as deliberately left out (e.g. skip{step:"select_template"}) so it is not repaired back in. Must be followed by an assertion of the block (expect_publish_blocked, attempt, expect_error, expect_message, expect_disabled).

steps.name: attempt
steps.purpose: NEGATIVE TESTS: try an action the case says the app must REFUSE, and pass only on positive evidence of the refusal — an error/warning toast, an inline message, a disabled control, or (expect:"nothing_opens") no drawer/dialog opening on a ready screen. Fails if the app allows it, and fails as 'could not tell' if the action broke for our own reasons. For a refused PUBLISH prefer expect_publish_blocked.

args.args: the inner step's args as an object, e.g. {role:"button", name:"Items"} for a click
args.because: substring the refusal message must contain (optional)
args.expect: "refused" (default: a message or a disabled control) | "nothing_opens"

steps.name: open_prepared
steps.purpose: FIRST STEP of a case whose starting state was built through the API: open the named screen on that event (no create, no publish, no search). Waits for the API calls that feed the screen and fails as 'could not tell' if they never come.

args.screen: one of: events_list | drafts_list | history_list | create | draft | proposal | summary | responses | overview | participants | analytics | technical | master_qcs

steps.name: expect_navigated
steps.purpose: Assert the browser is now on a named screen (after a click that should move it): the URL matches the screen's route and the screen is ready.

args.screen: one of: events_list | drafts_list | history_list | create | draft | proposal | summary | responses | overview | participants | analytics | technical | master_qcs
args.path: or: a substring the URL must contain

steps.name: expect_field_error
steps.purpose: Assert the app reports an error FOR a field: inline at the field (its form item / cell), or — as Procol often does — in an error message that names the field ("Please fill project title!" for Title). Optionally containing text. For a message that names no field, use expect_toast.

args.field: the field's label as on screen

steps.name: expect_toast
steps.purpose: Assert a toast appeared after the previous action — of a kind (success | error | warning | any), optionally containing text. Reads toasts that already faded.

steps.name: expect_api_value
steps.purpose: Assert the screen shows a value the API holds for this case's event — the event title, the vendor's name, the line item’s quantity and unit, the bid price and bid total — compared as a person reads it (₹, commas and .00 ignored).

steps.name: expect_order
steps.purpose: Assert order on screen: either the given texts appear in exactly this order, or the cells of a column/list (role+name/text) are sorted asc/desc (numbers compared as numbers).

args.items: array of texts in the expected order (optional)
args.text: a text every compared cell contains (optional)

steps.name: expect_screen_clean
steps.purpose: Assert the current screen passes the observation rules: no NaN / undefined / null / raw ids on screen, no server error or page crash since the previous look.

steps.name: expect_request
steps.purpose: Assert the screen SENT a request to the backend during this run (and how it was answered) — for cases that say "the screen calls GET /templates/…" or "POST /event_groups with …". Matches the request path (a fragment, ids may be left out), optionally its method, a query fragment and the answer status. Waits up to timeoutMs for it. It can check words in the request body (bodyContains / bodyLacks); sign-in calls are never recorded.

args.absent: true = assert the screen did NOT send it (optional)
args.bodyContains: word(s) the request body must carry, e.g. the remark text (optional)

steps.name: expect_qcs_vendors
steps.purpose: On Master QCS (after open_master_qcs or open_prepared master_qcs), assert the comparison grid's VENDOR COLUMNS: how many there are, which vendors they are, and that each is headed by a real company name, not a placeholder ("Vendor 1", "undefined", "-"). Use for "one column for the vendor", "both vendors appear", "the names are the real ones".

args.vendors: array of vendor names that must head a column (optional)
args.realNames: true (default) to fail on a placeholder column name

steps.name: expect_qcs_cell
steps.purpose: On Master QCS, read ONE cell of the comparison grid — a row ("Qty Offer", "Rank", "RFQ Rate", "RFQ Amount", "Sum Total", …) for one vendor column on one line item — and assert it. Compare with a fixed value, a number, or a value the API holds for this case (key). With no comparison it asserts the cell is filled. Row labels follow the template; the closest label is used and named in the result. A key (a value the API holds) exists only on a PREPARED state (open_prepared); in a plan that creates its own event, compare with number = the price the plan typed into place_surrogate_bid.

args.row: the row label as the screen shows it, e.g. "Rank", "Qty Offer", "RFQ Rate", "Sum Total"
args.vendor: vendor name or 1-based column number (optional; the only column, or the case's vendor)
args.product: substring of the line item's heading (optional; the first line item that has the row)
args.equals: exact text expected, as a person reads it — ₹, commas and spaces ignored (optional)
args.number: a number the CASE ITSELF states, e.g. 1 for Rank 1 (optional) — never a guessed figure: for the quantity, the price or the total use key
args.key: compare with a value the API holds: "quantity" (Qty Offer), "bidPrice" (the rate), "bidTotal" (the amount) (optional) — the way to check any figure the case says must equal the bid

steps.name: expect_qcs_amounts
steps.purpose: On Master QCS, check the arithmetic the grid shows: for each vendor and line item the amount equals rate × quantity, and the vendor's Sum Total equals the sum of its line amounts. Use for "Amount = price × quantity", "correct per-line and total amounts". Lines a vendor did not bid are skipped and named.

args.vendor: vendor name or 1-based column number (optional; every vendor column)
args.product: substring of one line item's heading (optional; every line item, and then the Sum Total too)
args.rate: row label of the unit price (optional; e.g. "RFQ Rate", found by default)
args.qty: row label of the quantity (optional; default "Qty Offer")
args.amount: row label of the line amount (optional; e.g. "RFQ Amount", found by default)
args.total: false to skip the Sum Total check (optional)

steps.name: expect_qcs_ranks
steps.purpose: On Master QCS, assert the ranks follow the amounts on every line item: on a buy event the lowest amount is Rank 1 and a higher amount never ranks better (order "highest" for a sell event). With one vendor it asserts that vendor is Rank 1. Use for "lowest total is rank 1", "ranks follow the amounts".

args.by: row label the ranks follow (optional; the line amount, e.g. "RFQ Amount")
args.product: substring of one line item's heading (optional)
args.atLeast: the case needs at least this many ranked vendors (optional; fewer = could not tell)

steps.name: search_participants
steps.purpose: On a PUBLISHED event's Participants list (open_prepared participants, or open_participants), type a vendor's name into "Search vendors" and wait for the list to narrow. Changes nothing on the event. Use before reading or acting on one vendor's row — the list is paginated, so a named vendor is usually not on page 1.

args.vendor: vendor name or email to search for (optional; the vendor select_participant added in this plan, else the case's own vendor)

steps.name: expect_participant
steps.purpose: On a published event's Participants list, search a vendor and assert ITS ROW (the name is read from the row, not from a button): that it is listed (present) or not, whether its box is ticked (selected = on this round), and whether it offers Add Bid. Use for "the vendor's row is visible with its Add Bid control", "the vendor appears in the selected list", "no Add Bid for this vendor". A vendor the case itself calls nonexistent or made up ("Acme Nonexistent Supplier") is never asserted present: assert the fallback instead — expect_participant_count{atLeast:1}, or present:false for that name.

args.vendor: vendor name or email (optional; the vendor select_participant added in this plan, else the case's own vendor)
args.present: true (default) the row must be listed; false it must not be
args.selected: true / false — the row's box must be ticked / unticked (optional)
args.addBid: true / false — the row must / must not offer Add Bid (optional)

steps.name: expect_participant_count
steps.purpose: On a published event's Participants list, count the vendors on this round — "Show only selected vendors" on, search cleared, every page — and assert the number. Use for "the count includes it", "the audience is not doubled", "exactly N participants".

args.grewBy: after select_participant: how many more than the round held before it (e.g. 1) — use this, not count, after adding a vendor (optional)

steps.name: select_participant
steps.purpose: On a published event's Participants list, add a vendor to the round: show every vendor, search it, tick its box (confirming if the app asks) and report what the app did. The vendor comes from the product's own list (the run may be set to QA test vendors only, and then refuses any other before clicking). Never invent a vendor name: name one only if the case does. Follow with expect_participant (no vendor = the one it added) and expect_participant_count{grewBy:1} — the round already holds the starting state's vendor, so never assert a fixed count after adding — or expect_error / expect_message for a refusal.

args.vendor: vendor name, only if the case gives a specific company name (optional). A case that names no specific company — "a vendor", "a known test vendor company" — leaves it out: the step adds a vendor from the product's own list not yet on the round, which is what such a case means
